newsitem.title: ITALY: Olivetti says won't divulge negotiations.
newsitem.headline: Olivetti says won't divulge negotiations.

text.p: Italian information technology group Olivetti said it could not divulge reserved information on negotiations underway on future divestments or strategic accords.
Olivetti said in a statement issued in response to detailed questions from market regulator Consob that the release of such reserved information could cause serious damage.

The group said it could not state its consolidated financial situation for the end of August 1996, as requested, until the first week of October "as in the practice of the company, justified by the necessary gathering of data coming from around 200 companies operating in the group."

Olivetti said the net asset value of stocks in the commercial warehouses of Olivetti Personal Computers at June 30 1996 was 198 billion lire, for Olivetti Lexikon 267 billion lire and for Olivetti Systems and Services 261 billion lire.

It said the average turnover of stock for Olivetti PCs was 1.5 months, three months for Lexikon and three months for Systems and Services "from which the realisable value of the goods in stock is evident".
Olivetti also said it had credits outstanding to the former Soviet Union of 134 billion lire in principal and 74 billion in interest.
It said the credits arose from the supply of an automated plant for the production of numerically controlled instruments.
The plant was built in St Petersburg in 1989.
Olivetti said it had conferred a mandate to Mediocredito Centrale to renegotiate the credit in the wider context of talks involving a number of Italian companies.

The company said it had heard from Mediocredito and other international banking organisations that the Russian authorities were expected to issue treasury paper in convertible currency by way of payment for the credits.
The paper should be issued shortly for repayment of the principal and by the end of 1997 for the payment of outstanding interest.
Olivetti ruled out the need to make further provisions for the credit in view of the "realistic possibility of obtaining payment in paper guaranteed in (hard) currency."
